hints: Look at the central atom in each hydride and think about its shape, not just its formula.
Count the bonding pairs and lone pairs on B in BH3, C in CH4 and C2H6, and N in NH3.
Remember that a lone pair repels more strongly than bonding pairs and squeezes the H-X-H angle down from the perfect tetrahedral angle.
walkthrough:
**Draw the electron-pair set up for each central atom**

Think side by side with me. The bond angle is decided by VSEPR, by how many electron pairs surround the central atom.

$\text{BH}_3$: 3 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. $\text{CH}_4$: 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$: each C has 4 bonding pairs, 0 lone pairs. $\text{NH}_3$: 3 bonding pairs, 1 lone pair.

**Predict the shape and ideal angle**

With no lone pairs, the pairs spread out as evenly as possible. $\text{BH}_3$ is trigonal planar with angle about $120^{\circ}$. $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ are tetrahedral with angle about $109.5^{\circ}$.

$$\text{repulsion strength: lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair}$$

**Apply the lone pair squeeze in ammonia**

$\text{NH}_3$ is also based on a tetrahedron of electron pairs, but one corner is a lone pair. That lone pair pushes harder and squeezes the three N-H bonds closer together.

$$\text{H-N-H in } \text{NH}_3 \approx 107^{\circ} < 109.5^{\circ} < 120^{\circ}$$

**Pick the smallest angle**

So $\text{NH}_3$ has the most compressed H-X-H angle of the four. That is the pyramidal molecule with the lone pair on nitrogen.

options.A: BH3 has only 3 electron pairs and no lone pair, so it is trigonal planar. Its H-B-H angle is about 120 degrees, the largest here, not the smallest.
options.B: CH4 has 4 bonding pairs and no lone pair, so it is perfectly tetrahedral. Its H-C-H angle is about 109.5 degrees, which is smaller than BH3 but still larger than a pyramidal molecule with a lone pair.
options.C: In C2H6 each carbon is bonded to 3 H atoms and 1 C atom, so 4 bonding pairs and no lone pair. Like methane it is tetrahedral at each carbon with angle about 109.5 degrees, so not the smallest.
options.D: NH3 has 3 bonding pairs plus 1 lone pair on nitrogen, giving a trigonal pyramidal shape. Lone pair to bond pair repulsion squeezes the H-N-H angle to about 107 degrees, the smallest of the four.
